CHIEF COMPLAINT
Patient presents to discuss smoking cessation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old patient presents motivated to quit smoking. Reports starting smoking in high school and progressing to daily use over the past several decades. Currently smoking one and a half packs per day, with first cigarette within one hour of waking. Previously attempted to quit by going cold turkey and was successful for almost one year, but relapsed during a period of work-related stress when layoffs occurred at his workplace. Patient recently joined the gym and has started meditation to help manage stress. Patient is highly motivated as he is expecting a daughter and wants to be present for her growing up. Patient reports friends have had success with nicotine patches and is interested in this smoking cessation aid. Patient has chosen next Monday (his birthday) as his quit date.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies other tobacco use. No acute complaints reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
History of gout
Systolic murmur (noted on prior exams)

MEDICATIONS
Allopurinol (for gout management)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Tobacco: Currently smoking 1.5 packs per day, started in high school, daily use for approximately 25+ years
Work: Recently experienced workplace stress related to layoffs; patient retained his position
Exercise: Recently joined gym
Stress management: Recently started meditation
Marital status: Married, expecting daughter any day
Other: Denies other tobacco products

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: BP 128/88, HR 68, RR 16, O2 saturation 98% on room air
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, 2/6 systolic murmur noted (known from prior exams, to continue monitoring)
Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally, no expiratory wheezes, no rales or rhonchi
Neck: No lymphadenopathy appreciated, no carotid bruits

RESULTS
Oxygen saturation and vital signs within normal limits

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine dependence: Counseled extensively on benefits of smoking cessation, particularly given history of type 2 diabetes and gout. Patient is highly motivated. Starting 21 mg nicotine patch on Monday (quit date). Instruct to change patch location daily to minimize skin irritation. Will taper dosage over time. Follow-up appointment in two weeks to reassess and adjust dosage as needed. Recommended stress management strategies including continued exercise, meditation, and yoga. Provided handouts regarding common smoking triggers. Will monitor stress levels related to work and upcoming birth of daughter.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Continue current management with diet and exercise. Will order hemoglobin A1c to be drawn prior to two-week follow-up appointment for monitoring.

3. History of gout: Continue allopurinol. Reinforce dietary modifications to avoid foods that exacerbate uric acid levels.

Follow-up appointment in two weeks.
